## Specific task description

Task instruction: Grasp the beige box with golden decoration and the black scanner with ergonomic handle simultaneously using separate arms, then scan.

Task description: The beige box with gold decoration is on the table's left and the black scanner with a curved handle on the right. Separate arms must hold them simultaneously, bringing the scanner close and aligning it with the box to scan.

Success criteria: Each arm holds either the box or scanner, with both grippers closed simultaneously. The box must be within close range directly ahead of the scanner's effective scanning point along its scanning direction and nearly aligned with the scanning axis, rather than merely near the side or back of the scanner head.

## Execution tips

- Consider grasping the box around the middle of its relatively flat opposite sides, away from corners, so the pads fit fully. Leave clearance on the side facing the scanner head.
- Grasp the scanner around a relatively straight section of the handle that can fit the full pads. Avoid the wide scanner head and curved end to reduce slipping and preserve room to approach the head for scanning.
- Set the opening slightly wider than the selected grasp width. Before closing, use different views to confirm that the fingers are actually on opposite sides rather than merely overlapping in the image.
- When adjusting the scanner orientation, consider using the open space in the middle of the table and leave clearance for the scanner head to turn, avoiding bottles behind it or the other gripper.
- When the scanning head approaches the box, consider holding one side steady while the other makes small angle and distance adjustments. Use multiple views to confirm front/back relationships and avoid large opposing arm motions that cause collisions.
